feedback: Approved to race. This candidate changes one controller field from iteration 1, ki from 0.0 to 0.5, and keeps base_speed 1.2, kp 1.5, kd 0.2, sensors at x = ±0.05 and last_direction. That isolates the integral term, which is the right test given the evidence. Iteration 1 (the best raced so far, 51.37, 0 finishes) showed max_error of 0.0609 on oval, 0.0645 on s-bend and 0.0621 on slalom, all just past the 0.06 m limit. Changing base_speed, kp and kd in iteration 0 to iteration 1 barely moved max_error (0.0614 to 0.0609), so speed and damping are not the main cause. Steering_oscillation stayed low (0.078 to 0.141), so jitter is not the cause either. A steady bias from the fixed left/right motor mismatch would fit this, and integral action is the reasonable tool for it. The candidate is valid, and the change is cheap and clearly bounded by the integral limit of ±2. It is the best-supported next step, so I am not revising it. Read the race results in this order. (1) If max_error falls below 0.05 on all three tracks with progress above 0.5, the bias hypothesis holds. (2) If max_error stays near 0.06 with ki 0.5, the error is probably a start transient or an early overshoot. (3) If s-bend or slalom max_error rises while the oval improves, the integral is winding up on the tighter bends, so the next test should lower ki (for example to 0.2) rather than raise it.
requested_changes: If max_error falls below 0.05 on all tracks and progress is above 0.5, raise controller.base_speed in steps of 0.2 (1.2 to 1.4, then 1.6) with ki kept at 0.5, kp 1.5 and kd 0.2, so the speed effect is isolated. Iteration 1 showed base_speed changes alone did not move max_error.

If max_error stays at about 0.06 on all tracks with ki 0.5, the swing is likely a start transient rather than a steady bias. Test controller.kd at 0.4 with ki 0.5, since iteration 1 showed kd 0.05 to 0.2 gave no clear change, or test a sharper line_loss response (search_left or search_right) only if line_loss_events stays at 1 per run.

If s-bend or slalom max_error rises above 0.065 while the oval improves, integral windup on the tighter bends is the likely cause. Lower controller.ki to 0.2 and keep the other fields the same, so the windup effect is isolated.
